Subject: Re: Thanks — quick clarifying Qs after today's demo

Kate — great questions. Short recap and proposed pathway below. I pasted a suggested runbook at the end with primary owners.

1) Recommended starting variants
- Controlled baseline: your current elastic/ranker (we'll call it BrightCart-Prod) as control.
- Redwood candidate A: redwood/rank-lite-v2 (8-bit quantized, optimized for tail latency).
- Redwood candidate B: redwood/rerank-deep-1 (higher-context reranker, slower but stronger for long-tail).

Rationale: v2 is low-cost, low-risk — good to validate latency/cost delta. rerank-deep-1 targets the long-tail quality wins you saw in the demo.

2) Quick benchmark (on the sample queries you attached)
- NDCG@10: BrightCart-Prod = 0.412; redwood/rank-lite-v2 = 0.433; redwood/rerank-deep-1 = 0.473
- MRR: BrightCart-Prod = 0.318; redwood/rank-lite-v2 = 0.335; redwood/rerank-deep-1 = 0.386

Summary: both Redwood candidates show measurable lift on the sample set. Detailed CSV and per-query deltas attached (ndcg_mrr_summary.csv). These numbers are on a dev snapshot — we'll re-run in your staging environment for a more accurate baseline.

3) Quality regression risks to watch during A/B
- Prompt drift: subtle changes in query normalization cause upstream prompts to trigger different ranking heuristics.
- Entity hallucination in long queries: extreme prompts can surface less relevant items if prompt templates aren't constrained.
- Cold-category variance: categories with sparse training data can show noisy MRR swings.

Monitoring hooks we recommend: per-category NDCG, top-k movement heatmaps, and a small human-eval daily sample (50 queries) for precision checks. Redwood Console can emit regression alerts tied to saved prompt sets.

4) A/B design (2-week staging)
- 1 week small-sample canary (5% traffic in staging): compare BrightCart-Prod vs rank-lite-v2 for latency/cost sanity.
- 2nd week: expand to 20% and introduce rerank-deep-1 as an asynchronous reranker for a subset (re-ranked results surfaced to internal QA only).
- Success criteria: NDCG lift >= +0.03 and no category showing >10% regression in precision; latency P95 within your SLA (+50ms of baseline).

5) Owners and next steps
- Laura Bennett (me): technical pilot owner, coordinate model provisioning and dev-side run.
- Marissa Cole: eval kit & prompt set preparation (will deliver the prompt pack + evaluation harness by Tue EOD).
- Sergio Alvarez: commercial owner — finalize pilot SOW and pricing for dedicated canary capacity.
- Karthik Iyer: solutions engineering — on-call for deployment and canary instrumentation.

Links & artifacts:
- Benchmark repo: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/brightcart/benchmarks/2027-05-15 (ndcg_mrr_summary.csv attached)
- Prompt pack: brightcart_prompt_set_v1.json (attached)
- Pilot runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.com/pilot-runbooks/brightcart-canary

I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to lock the pilot scope unless you prefer a different cadence.

Best,
Laura Bennett
